observed_vs_expected: Consistent with early-phase hypothesis validation. Round 1 yields a best_target_score of 0.7109, establishing the baseline for the chirp_rate sweep. The expectation that the score should increase as chirp parameters span the 300-450 nm band cannot yet be longitudinally verified with a single execution, but the immediate physical response aligns: layer thicknesses actively expand into the target modulation range (up to ~359 nm). No contradictory deviation is detected; rather, the data confirms the route is operational and probing the intended spectral region.
deviation_mechanism: The physical bottleneck driving the current score ceiling is asymmetric parameter activation within the candidate pool. Candidate 0 maintains rigid 200.0/270.0 nm layer alternation across all 20 indices, indicating a failure of the optimizer to couple the chirp_rate variable to this population member's optical path lengths. Conversely, Candidates 1 and 2 physically engaged the chirp degrees of freedom, stretching individual layers into the 128–359 nm regime (e.g., Candidate 2, Layer 10: 359.48 nm; Candidate 1, Layer 2: 356.58 nm). This bifurcation means only two-thirds of the search space is dynamically exploring the designed wavelength-scanning mechanism, artificially suppressing aggregate merit while the third candidate acts as a fixed-period anchor.
continue_rationale: Only 1 round has been executed against the mandatory 2-round floor for exhaustion evaluation. The current best_target_score of 0.7109 with 9 valid candidates demonstrates active exploration and survival of diverse morphologies. Stopping now would discard critical early chirp-response data before determining whether the score trajectory continues upward, plateaus below the 1e-3 gain threshold, or triggers the boundary-limit reversal protocol defined in the stop conditions.
insight_for_next: Force symmetric exploration by reinitializing Candidate 0 with a deterministic chirped seed (linear thickness increment of +6 nm per pair starting from 210 nm baseline) instead of its current fixed periodicity. Concurrently, apply localized thickness jitter (+/- 20 nm) specifically to layers exceeding 320 nm in Candidates 1 and 2 to disrupt potential Fabry-Pérot resonance traps and probe adjacent transmission windows near the 300-450 nm target band.
insight_grounding: This plan directly addresses the measured asymmetry in Round 1: Candidate 0's thickness array `[200.0, 270.0, 200.0, 270.0, ...]` contains zero variation despite 9 surviving candidates, whereas Candidate 2 reaches 359.48 nm at Layer 10 and Candidate 1 reaches 356.58 nm at Layer 2. The score of 0.7109 remains capped precisely because one population slot contributes a non-chirped, static optical stack, limiting the effective bandwidth coverage and preventing full exploitation of the 300-450 nm design space.
